title: Heavy rain before autumn sampling lowered English river invertebrate scores more where storm overflows discharge into the same water body (1991-2024), but not in spring and not before 2008
abstract: Question: does heavy rain lower English river invertebrate quality more where storm overflows discharge into the same Water Framework Directive water body? Data: Environment Agency kick samples 1991-2024 (59,745 autumn and 58,943 spring samples, about 5,500 sites, 2,800 water bodies), storm overflow outlets from EDM annual returns 2021-2025 (14,808 outlets), E-OBS daily rain, GHSL built-up fraction. Method: within-site models with EA-area x year effects; exposure = days with at least 10 mm rain in the 28 days before the sample (H28) x log2(1 + overflow outlets in the water body); plan written before the fits. Results: in autumn, the interaction was -0.0025 WHPT ASPT per rain day per doubling of outlets (95% CI -0.0042 to -0.0007; permutation p = 0.007). Per heavy-rain day, ASPT changed by -0.0023 (CI -0.0065 to 0.0020) with no outlet and by -0.0121 (CI -0.0174 to -0.0069) with 15 outlets. The autumn result stayed with urban, river-size, altitude and site-quality rain interactions and with investigative or log-abundance samples, and a placebo with rain after the sample was null. It was clear in 2008-2024 (-0.0052) but zero in 1991-2007, and negative but uncertain in each of four regions. In spring the interaction was null (-0.0004, CI -0.0030 to 0.0022). Annual spill hours rose 2.8% per heavy-rain day. Limitations: association only; outlet locations from 2021-2025 applied to all years; downstream outlets in the same water body count; a direct 2021-2024 spill-hours test was too short to resolve.

Bars: 95% intervals of bin means. Autumn samples fall more after rain where overflows exist; spring samples do not.
Rain x overflow interaction (H28 x log2(1 + outlets)) with 95% CIs for all planned tests and two post-hoc periods. Orange: CI below zero. Grey: placebo with rain after the sample.

Left: observed interactions (lines) against 300 within-area shuffles of overflow counts. Right: mean number of heavy-rain days in fixed 28-day spring and autumn windows at sampled site cells, 1991-2024, with linear trends (autumn trend uncertain).
